newsitem.title: QATAR: Qatar's Rasgas says secures $2.55 bln financing.
newsitem.headline: Qatar's Rasgas says secures $2.55 bln financing.

text.p: Qatar's Ras Laffan Liquefied Natural Gas Co (Rasgas) said on Sunday it had concluded arrangements for $2.55 billion in loans and bonds to finance a $3.4 billion LNG project.
"The financing includes $1.35 billion in loan facilities and $1.2 billion in bond offerings," said Khalid al-Hajri, acting managing director of the company.

Rasgas' finance manager John Coombs told reporters the loan package included a $450 million facility arranged by a syndicate of international banks led by the Industrial Bank of Japan and Credit Suisse.

It also included a $465 million loan facility supported by the Export-Import (EXIM) Bank of the United States, $250 million by Britain's Export Credit Guarantee Department (ECGD) and $185 million by SACE, Italy's export credit agency.
Goldman Sachs and CS First Boston, joint lead managers of the bond issue, had announced the launch of two bonds worth a total of $1.2 billion on December 12.
Rasgas is one of the oil and gas-rich Gulf Arab state's three major gas export projects designed to exploit its mammoth gas reserves -- the third largest in the world after Russia's and Iran's.
It is 66.5 percent owned by the state's Qatar General Petroleum Corporation, 26.5 percent by the United States' Mobil Corp, four percent by Japan's Nissho Iwai and three percent by Itochu Corp.

"The financing represents part of the funding for the first phase of Rasgas' multi-billion-dollar gas liquefaction project designed to produce 5.2 million tonnes a year of LNG from two trains of 2.6 million tonne capacity each," al-Hajri said.
The remaining cost -- equivalent to around 30 percent, or $850 million -- will be met by shareholder equity contribution.
Coombs said the bond issues -- $400 million of 10-year duration and $800 million of 17 1/2 years duration -- were unique in the industry and the Middle East.

"The bond offering represents the first capital market issue for an LNG project, the first debt offering for any Qatari entity and the first Middle Eastern debt issue with a maturity beyond seven years," he said.

The Rasgas project is scheduled to go on on stream in July 1999. Rasgas has signed a 25-year sales and purchase agreement with South Korea's Korean Gas Corporation to supply 2.4 million tonnes of LNG annually from mid-1999 and is negotiating further deals with other customers in the Far East and Asia.
Eventually, the project is due for "staged expansion up to a 6-train capacity, or 15.6 million tonnes annually, to meet future LNG market demand", al-Hajri said.

Qatar's other gas export projects include Qatar Liquefied Gas Company (Qatargas), which went on stream in September, and Qatar-Enron LNG Marketing Company, which is expected to start production in 2001.
